tools.name: read_wiki
tools.description: Who is signed in (username, role) and which wiki features are on (revisions, link refactoring, upload size).

tools.name: read_tree
tools.description: Page hierarchy as indented lines with path and id, for the whole wiki or below one page.

under.description: Page id or path to list below; omit for the whole wiki

depth.description: Levels shown, default 3; deeper ones are counted

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: One page: Markdown content, tags, properties, authors and the version needed to change it.

tools.name: read_lookup_path
tools.description: Check a wiki path without changing anything: for each segment whether it exists (and its id), and whether the whole path exists or can be created. To create the missing segments, use write_ensure_path.

path.description: Wiki path like docs/team/onboarding; slashes at either end are ignored

tools.name: read_find_title
tools.description: Pages whose title matches exactly (case-insensitive), with path and id.

title.description: Whole title to match, in any case

tools.name: read_search
tools.description: Full-text search over page titles, content and tags, best match first, with excerpts. Use it to find pages by the words in them; for an exact title use read_find_title, for pages carrying given tags read_pages_by_tags.

offset.description: Results to skip, for the next page of hits

tools.name: read_search_status
tools.description: Report the search index: whether it is still building (active), how many pages are indexed or failed, and when it last finished. Check it when read_search misses a page that was just changed.

tools.name: read_tags
tools.description: List the tags in use, each with how many pages carry it. To find the pages that carry given tags, use read_pages_by_tags.

tools.name: read_pages_by_tags
tools.description: List the pages that carry every one of the given tags, with id, path, title, tags and last change. For the tags in use, use read_tags; for free text, read_search.

tags.description: Tags a page must all carry

tools.name: read_properties
tools.description: List the property keys in use (key-value page metadata, e.g. owner), each with how many pages set it. To find the pages, use read_pages_by_property.

tools.name: read_pages_by_property
tools.description: List the pages that set a property key, optionally only those with one value, with id, path, title, their properties and last change. For the keys in use, use read_properties.

value.description: Only pages with exactly this value; omit for any

tools.name: read_links
tools.description: Show a page's links: pages that link to it, pages it links to, and broken links in both directions. Use it before moving or deleting a page; read_broken_links covers the whole wiki.

tools.name: read_broken_links
tools.description: List every broken link in the wiki: the linking page's path and id, and the missing target. Admins only (others get status 403); for one page, use read_links.

tools.name: read_revisions
tools.description: A page's revision history, newest first (needs revisions on).

tools.name: read_revision
tools.description: Read one past revision of a page: who made it, when, and the full Markdown content at that time. Get revision ids from read_revisions; to see what changed, use read_compare_revisions.

tools.name: read_compare_revisions
tools.description: Line diff between two revisions of a page, or between one revision and the latest.

target.description: Newer revision id; omit for the latest

tools.name: read_favorites
tools.description: List the signed-in user's favorite pages with id, path, title and version. Add or remove them with write_favorite.

tools.name: read_assets
tools.description: List the files attached to a page: name, the path to use in Markdown links, and the absolute URL. Attach with write_upload_asset; rename or delete with write_rename_asset and delete_asset.

tools.name: read_slug
tools.description: Suggest the slug (URL segment) LeafWiki would derive from a title, unique under the parent; changes nothing. Editors only. write_create_page and write_copy already do this when slug is omitted.

title.description: Title to derive the slug from

parent.description: Parent id or path; omit for the top level

tools.name: read_refactor_preview
tools.description: Which pages link to a page and would be rewritten if it were renamed or moved (needs link refactoring on); changes nothing.

parent.description: New parent id or path (move); "/" for the top level

tools.name: write_create_page
tools.description: Create a page, or a section (a folder-like page for children), under a parent, optionally with content, tags and properties; answers with its id, path and version. To create a whole missing path at once, use write_ensure_path.

parent.description: Parent id or path; omit for the top level

slug.description: URL segment; omit to derive it from the title

kind.description: section: a folder-like page for children

tags.description: Full tag list, replaces the current one

properties.description: Full property map, replaces the current one

tools.name: write_ensure_path
tools.description: Make sure a path exists, creating every missing segment; the last one gets the title.

kind.description: Of the last segment; section: a folder-like page for children

tools.name: write_update_page
tools.description: Change a page's title, slug, content, tags or properties; fields you leave out stay as they are.

version.description: version from your last read of the page

slug.description: New URL segment; changes the path, which can break links

tags.description: Full tag list, replaces the current one

properties.description: Full property map, replaces the current one

tools.name: write_edit_text
tools.description: Replace one exact passage of a page's content, without sending the whole page.

version.description: version from your last read of the page

find.description: Exact text, occurring once in the page

replace.description: New text; empty removes the passage

tools.name: write_append
tools.description: Add Markdown at the end of a page, after a blank line; the rest stays as it is. Needs no version: it appends to the latest one. To change existing text, use write_edit_text.

tools.name: write_tags
tools.description: Add or remove tags on a page, keeping its other tags; answers with the new tag list. To replace the whole list, use write_update_page.

tools.name: write_properties
tools.description: Set or remove properties (key-value page metadata) on a page, keeping the others; answers with the new properties. To replace them all, use write_update_page.

tools.name: write_move
tools.description: Move a page (with its children) under another parent; links to it are not rewritten (see write_refactor).

parent.description: New parent id or path; "/" for the top level

position.description: Index among the new siblings; default last

tools.name: write_sort
tools.description: Reorder the children of a page, or the top level; answers with the ids in their new order. Pages keep their parent: to move one elsewhere, use write_move.

parent.description: Parent id or path; "/" for the top level

order.description: Every child id or path, in the new order

tools.name: write_pin
tools.description: Pin a page so it stays above its unpinned siblings in the tree, or unpin it; answers with the page.

tools.name: write_favorite
tools.description: Add a page to the signed-in user's favorites, or remove it; only that user sees them. List them with read_favorites.

tools.name: write_convert
tools.description: Turn an existing page into a section (a folder-like page that holds children) or a section into a page; answers with the page. Use it when a page should get children; to create a new section, use write_create_page with kind section. A section that still has children stays one: move them out first with write_move.

kind.description: section: a folder-like page for children

tools.name: write_copy
tools.description: Copy a page's content, tags, properties and files to a new page with a new title under a parent; the original stays. Answers with the copy's id and path.

parent.description: Parent id or path; omit for the top level

slug.description: URL segment; omit to derive it from the title

tools.name: write_refactor
tools.description: Rename or move a page and rewrite the links that point to it (needs link refactoring on; preview with read_refactor_preview).

version.description: version from your last read of the page

parent.description: New parent id or path (move); "/" for the top level

position.description: Index among the new siblings; default last

tools.name: write_restore_revision
tools.description: Bring a page back to a past revision (the current state stays in the history).

tools.name: write_upload_asset
tools.description: Attach a file to a page from base64 data; answers with the Markdown link to embed it.

filename.description: Name to store it under, e.g. diagram.png

base64.description: File content as base64; local paths are not read

tools.name: write_rename_asset
tools.description: Rename a file attached to a page; answers with its new path and URL. Links to the old name in page content are not updated: fix them with write_edit_text.

from.description: Current file name, as read_assets lists it

tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: Delete a page; a page with children is refused unless recursive is true.

version.description: version from your last read of the page

recursive.description: Also delete every page below it; only when the user asked for that

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Delete a file attached to a page. Links to it in page content are not removed and will break; read_assets lists the files.

filename.description: File name, as read_assets lists it
